# Binary test fixtures

Files that cannot be generated by the libraries Forge depends on.

## `locked-hunter2.pdf`

A 3-page PDF encrypted with AES-256. **User password: `hunter2`.**

It is checked in rather than generated because nothing in the dependency set
can *write* an encrypted PDF: `pdf-lib` has no encryption support, and PDFium
can open a locked document but exposes no save function. The alternative was a
hand-rolled RC4/Standard-Security-Handler writer in a test helper, which is a
lot of bespoke cryptography to maintain for one fixture.

It was produced by mupdf during a spike, before that dependency was removed for
being AGPL-3.0-or-later (see the phase 4a design doc, Amendment 1). A PDF
emitted by a tool is not a derivative work of that tool, so this file carries no
licence obligation — the same way a document is not encumbered by the editor
that wrote it.

Verified against PDFium: rejected with no password
(`Password required or incorrect password`), opens with `hunter2`, 3 pages.

## `text/`

PDF text-extraction fixtures for spec §4.1: `columns.pdf`, `hebrew.pdf`,
`arabic.pdf`, `cjk.pdf` and `ligatures.pdf`, each one page. The text drawn on
each page is in `manifest.json`, which the tests read as ground truth.

Generated once on macOS by CoreText, which lays out right-to-left scripts,
CJK and ligatures the way a Mac app's "Save as PDF" does:

    swift scripts/make-text-fixtures.swift tests/fixtures/text/manifest.json tests/fixtures/text

They embed subsets of macOS system fonts, as any PDF saved on a Mac does.
They are test data only and never ship (`files` in package.json is `dist`).
The Type3 and scanned cases are built at test time instead
(`makeType3Pdf`, `makeScannedPdf` in `tests/helpers/fixtures.ts`).

## `heic/small.heic`

A 64×48 HEVC-in-HEIF image, so the Windows job can exercise the `heic`
extension (Windows spec §5.3) — Windows has no `sips` to make one at test
time. The pixels are a gradient: red ramps 0→255 left to right, green 0→255
top to bottom, blue fixed at 128. Made once on macOS:

    # in.png: a 64×48 RGB PNG of that gradient, written by Sharp from a raw buffer
    sips -s format heic in.png --out tests/fixtures/heic/small.heic

`sips` encodes with Apple's own HEVC codec, as an iPhone does. Opaque, no
rotation, a single tile.
